test.name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties - Test 2

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange Be, Mg, Ca in order of increasing atomic radius.

text_solutions: Atomic radius increases down a group due to additional electron shells. For group 2: Be < Mg < Ca.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the third period has the highest second ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy is highest when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X+}\) ion. Na (after losing one electron, becomes \(\ce{Na+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value in period 3 compared to Mg, Si, or P.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which ion among the following isoelectronic species with 10 electrons has the lowest ionic radius?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (10 electrons), ionic radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{Al^3+}\) (Z=13) has the lowest radius compared to \(\ce{Na+}\), \(\ce{Mg^2+}\), or \(\ce{F^-}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 15 has the highest electronegativity?

text_solutions: Electronegativity decreases down group 15. N (period 2, 3.0) has the highest value among N, P, As, and Sb.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element forms an acidic oxide predominant in group 15?

text_solutions: Group 15 elements form acidic oxides, especially higher oxides. P forms \(\ce{P2O5}\), which is acidic, unlike Be (basic), Ca (basic), or Zn (amphoteric).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the third period has the highest fourth ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Fourth ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X^3+}\) ion. Al (after losing three electrons, becomes \(\ce{Al^3+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value in period 3.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 17 element forms the strongest hydrogen bonds in its hydride?

text_solutions: Hydrogen bonding strength depends on electronegativity and size. F (in \(\ce{HF}\)) forms the strongest hydrogen bonds due to its high electronegativity (4.0) and small size, unlike Cl, Br, or I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which d-block element in period 4 has the highest density?

text_solutions: In period 4 d-block (Sc to Zn), density increases with atomic mass and decreases with volume. Cu (group 11) has the highest density due to its compact structure.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the ground state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^3 4s^2\)?

text_solutions: This configuration (Z=23) corresponds to V (period 4, group 5), with \(3d^3 4s^2\), distinguishing it from Ti (\(3d^2 4s^2\)), Cr (\(3d^5 4s^1\)), or Mn (\(3d^5 4s^2\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements exhibits a diagonal relationship with Be?

text_solutions: Be (group 2, period 2) shows a diagonal relationship with Al (group 13, period 3) due to similar size and electronegativity, unlike Mg, Ca, or B.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 16 element forms a hydride with the lowest boiling point?

text_solutions: Boiling points of group 16 hydrides increase with molecular weight, except for \(\ce{H2O}\) (hydrogen bonding). \(\ce{H2S}\) has the lowest boiling point among \(\ce{H2O}\), \(\ce{H2S}\), \(\ce{H2Se}\), and \(\ce{H2Te}\) due to weak intermolecular forces.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 16 has the lowest first ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy decreases down a group due to increasing size. Among O, S, Se, and Te, Te (period 5) has the lowest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a metalloid?

text_solutions: Metalloids lie along the metal-non-metal boundary. Si (group 14) is a metalloid, while Na (group 1), Mg (group 2), and S (group 16) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest third ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a noble gas-like \(\ce{X^2+}\) ion. Ca (after losing two electrons, becomes \(\ce{Ca^2+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6\)) has the highest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 2 has the highest second ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy for group 2 elements involves removing an electron from \(\ce{X+}\) (noble gas-like). Be⁺ (smallest size) has the highest value due to greater nuclear attraction.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element was predicted as Eka-silicon by Mendeleev?

text_solutions: Mendeleev predicted Eka-silicon below Si, later identified as Germanium (Ge), matching its properties like oxide formula \(\ce{GeO2}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an s-block element?

text_solutions: s-block elements have outermost electrons in s-orbitals (groups 1 and 2). Na (group 1) is an s-block element, while B (group 13), Si (group 14), and P (group 15) are p-block elements.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following elements in order of decreasing second ionization enthalpy: Li, Be, B, C.

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy is highest for Li (removing e⁻ from \(\ce{Li+}\) with \(1s^2\)) and decreases across period 2 as stability reduces: Li > Be > B > C.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fifth period has the highest sixth ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Sixth ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X^5+}\) ion. Te (after losing five electrons, becomes \(\ce{Te^5+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^6\)) has the highest value in period 5.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following elements in order of decreasing electron affinity: F, Cl, Br, I.

text_solutions: Electron affinity decreases down group 17, with Cl highest due to optimal size and nuclear charge, followed by F (anomaly due to repulsion). Order: Cl > F > Br > I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 15 forms a pentoxide with the highest thermal stability?

text_solutions: Thermal stability of group 15 pentoxides (\(\ce{X2O5}\)) decreases down the group due to weaker X-O bonds. \(\ce{N2O5}\) is the most stable thermally, decomposing at a higher temperature than \(\ce{P2O5}\), \(\ce{As2O5}\), or \(\ce{Sb2O5}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the highest third ionization enthalpy among the following?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy is highest when removing an electron from a noble gas-like configuration. Mg (after losing two electrons, becomes \(\ce{Mg^2+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value.

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from the same group shows the greatest increase in atomic radius?

text_solutions: Atomic radius increases down a group, with the largest jump often between early periods. In group 1, Li (period 2) to Na (period 3) shows a significant increase due to the addition of a new shell, compared to later pairs.

qns_content.text: Which element in group 15 has the highest tendency to form stable compounds in the +3 oxidation state?

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the ground state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^1\)?

text_solutions: This configuration (Z=31) corresponds to Ga (period 4, group 13), with \(4p^1\) distinguishing it from Zn (\(4p^0\)), Ge (\(4p^2\)), or As (\(4p^3\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 13 has the lowest third ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy decreases down group 13 as size increases, reducing nuclear attraction. Tl (period 6) has the lowest value among B, Al, Ga, and Tl.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed between aluminium and sulfur?

text_solutions: Al (group 13, valence 3) and S (group 16, valence 2) form \(\ce{Al2S3}\) by cross-multiplying valences, a stable ionic compound.

qns_content.text: Which group 17 element exhibits the least reactivity with hydrogen due to its bond strength?

text_solutions: Reactivity with hydrogen decreases down group 17 as H-X bond strength weakens. F forms the strongest H-F bond, making \(\ce{HF}\) the least reactive among HF, HCl, HBr, and HI.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group contains only p-block elements?

text_solutions: p-block spans groups 13–18. Options: (1) Na (group 1), Mg (group 2) → s-block; (2) B (group 13), C (group 14) → p-block; (3) Li (group 1), Be (group 2) → s-block; (4) K (group 1), Ca (group 2) → s-block.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed by carbon and chlorine?

text_solutions: C (group 14, valence 4) and Cl (group 17, valence 1) form \(\ce{CCl4}\) by sharing electrons to achieve stable configurations.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 17 shows an anomaly in electron gain enthalpy compared to its neighbors?

text_solutions: F has less negative electron gain enthalpy than Cl due to electron repulsion in its compact 2p orbitals, an anomaly in group 17 trends where Cl > Br > I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 16 element forms a dioxide that exists as a linear gas at room temperature?

text_solutions: In group 16, \(\ce{O2}\) is a linear diatomic gas at room temperature, unlike \(\ce{SO2}\) (bent), \(\ce{SeO2}\) (polymeric solid), or \(\ce{TeO2}\) (solid).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the electronic configuration ending in \(4s^2 4p^3\) in its ground state?

text_solutions: The configuration \(4s^2 4p^3\) corresponds to As (Z=33, period 4, group 15), with full configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^3\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 13 element forms a trioxide with the highest acidity?

text_solutions: Acidity of group 13 trioxides decreases down the group. \(\ce{B2O3}\) (B, smallest) is the most acidic, forming boric acid, unlike \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (amphoteric), \(\ce{Ga2O3}\), or \(\ce{In2O3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 13 has the highest ionization enthalpy after losing two electrons?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy is highest for B (removing an electron from \(\ce{B^2+}\) with \(1s^2\)) due to its small size and stable configuration, compared to Al, Ga, or In.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the smallest ionic radius among the following cations?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic cations (\(\ce{Li+}\), \(\ce{Be^2+}\), \(\ce{B^3+}\), \(\ce{C^4+}\), all with 2 electrons), radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{B^3+}\) (Z=5) is smaller than \(\ce{Li+}\) (Z=3), \(\ce{Be^2+}\) (Z=4), and \(\ce{C^4+}\) (Z=6).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a fourth period element reacts with both acids and bases?

text_solutions: In period 4, \(\ce{ZnO}\) (from Zn, group 12) is amphoteric, reacting with acids (e.g., HCl) and bases (e.g., NaOH), unlike \(\ce{K2O}\) (basic), \(\ce{GeO2}\) (acidic), or \(\ce{As2O3}\) (acidic).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest boiling point among d-block elements?

text_solutions: In period 4 d-block (Sc to Zn), boiling point peaks with strong metallic bonding. Cr (group 6) has the highest boiling point due to its \(3d^5 4s^1\) configuration and maximum unpaired electrons enhancing bonding.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 17 element is the most stable in its highest oxidation state?

text_solutions: Stability of group 17 oxides in high oxidation states increases down the group. \(\ce{I2O5}\) (I, +5) is the most stable, unlike \(\ce{F2O}\), \(\ce{Cl2O7}\), or \(\ce{BrO3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide is acidic in nature?

text_solutions: Oxides of non-metals (right side of periodic table) are acidic. \(\ce{SO3}\) (group 16) is acidic, while \(\ce{Na2O}\) (group 1), \(\ce{MgO}\) (group 2), and \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (group 13, amphoteric) are not purely acidic.

text_solutions: P (group 15, valence 5 in +5 state) forms \(\ce{P2O5}\) with oxygen (valence 2), a stable acidic oxide.

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy for group 1 elements involves removing an electron from \(\ce{X+}\) (noble gas configuration). Cs⁺ (largest size) has the lowest value due to reduced nuclear attraction.

qns_content.text: Which group 15 element forms a trichloride with the highest covalent character?

text_solutions: Covalent character (Fajans’ rule) increases with smaller size and higher charge density. \(\ce{NCl3}\) (N, smallest) has the highest covalent character among N, P, As, and Sb trichlorides.
